The agency's own records, not this company's, would hold such requests, and the answered 2026-04-01 call may be where one was made, but its content is not logged. policy.text:
# Internal Policy: General Dispute Handling Process

**Applies to:** Any complaint not governed more specifically by another policy in this set (i.e., the default process).

## Standard process
1. **Acknowledge** receipt within 3 business days.
2. **Investigate** — compare the customer's claim against account and transaction records.
3. **Classify** the outcome as one of: confirmed (company error), not confirmed (no error found), partially confirmed (mixed), or unable to verify (insufficient data).
4. **Respond** in writing within 15 calendar days of receipt (consistent with standard regulatory complaint-handling expectations), addressing every distinct allegation raised in the complaint individually — a response that addresses only the primary complaint and ignores a secondary request is incomplete.
5. **Close** the case with a documented root-cause category for internal trend reporting.

## What counts as a complete response
- Every distinct factual allegation is addressed (confirmed, not confirmed, or unable to verify).
- Every distinct request the customer made is addressed (a refund request and an account-closure request in the same complaint both need a response, even if only one is granted).
- The response states a clear next step or outcome — never ends on an open-ended "we are looking into it" with no indication of what happens next, unless the case is genuinely still pending additional information.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state what was investigated and the outcome in plain language.
- May NOT close a case as "resolved" if any raised allegation was not actually addressed.

## Escalation trigger
Use the dedicated Escalation Criteria policy (document 09) for attorney/regulator/vulnerability triggers. This document covers only the baseline process for complaints that don't meet those triggers.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
Getting four or five calls a day about a payday loan, and feeling too afraid to pick up the phone, is stressful, and we understand why you wrote to us. Here's what we found on each part of your complaint.

The number of calls: The call records we reviewed match what you described. There were 4 calls on March 30, 2026 and 5 calls on March 31, 2026. There was also a call on April 1, 2026 at 12:05 that lasted 2 minutes.

Calls before 8am: Two of those calls came in early, one at 7:41 on March 30 and one at 7:55 on March 31. The records list call times but don't show a time zone. If those times don't match when your phone actually rang, please tell us.

Your requests to be contacted only by mail: We looked through your account history and didn't find a record of a request for mail-only contact. The only mail contact on file is a notice dated March 2, 2026. The records also don't show what was said on the April 1 call. We aren't saying you didn't ask. We just can't confirm it from the records we have.

Your worry about answering the phone: We've taken this on board, and it's part of what we're passing on with your request.

What happens next: Because we can't confirm that a mail-only request was made, we can't tell you today that the calls will switch to mail. We're referring your request for mail-only contact for review, and we can't promise what the outcome will be.

It would help if you could tell us when and how you asked for mail-only contact. The dates, whether it was by phone or in writing, and the name of anyone you spoke to would all be useful. If you have letters, texts, or notes about the calls, please send them too. You're welcome to send us anything further at any time, and we'll review it. You can reply to this message or call the number on your account.

Case reference: 20962593.

verifier.groundedness_check: fail — the draft says of the customer's fear of answering the phone: "We've taken this on board, and it's part of what we're passing on with your request." This claims an action (passing the fear concern on) that the verification output does not support. `referral_stated` covers only the mail-only request, the call frequency, and the before-8am calls, and does not include the customer's fear. The human reviewer would therefore not know to carry out this referral, so the statement could be untrue when sent. Separately, the draft's other referral ("We're referring your request for mail-only contact for review") is declared in `referral_stated`. But the verification output confirms no error, and the exception for referral statements covers refunds and corrections, so the reviewer should confirm that a review path for mail-only requests actually exists. All dates, call counts, call times, the 2-minute April 1 call, and the March 2 notice trace correctly to the verification output.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — no remedy is stated (`remedy_stated` is null). The draft promises no outcome and expressly says it cannot promise what the outcome will be. No fee waiver, refund, or account change is offered.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — no fault admission beyond confirmed fact (the call count and the two before-8am calls are stated as confirmed facts only). No future guarantees: "we can't tell you today that the calls will switch to mail" and "we can't promise what the outcome will be" avoid promising anything. No legal conclusions, and nothing discourages the customer from other channels.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — the draft follows Policy 11's order: an opening that references the specific complaint, findings per allegation in separate short paragraphs, an outcome/next-steps section, and the case reference 20962593 at the end. The tone is plain and direct, with no marketing content. The length is acceptable for a multi-allegation complaint.
specific_issues: Groundedness: "it's part of what we're passing on with your request" asserts that the customer's fear of answering the phone is being passed on, but `referral_stated` does not include it. Either add the fear concern to `referral_stated` or remove or reword the sentence so it makes no action claim.
Reviewer note: confirm that a review path for mail-only contact requests exists before sending, since the verification output does not establish one.

draft.draft_text:
You told us a collection agency has been calling you four or five times a day about a payday loan, that some of the calls come before 8am, and that you've asked more than once to be contacted only by mail. Dreading the phone to the point of being afraid to answer it is stressful, and we're glad you wrote to us.

Here is what we found, one point at a time.

The number of calls: Our call records match what you described. They show 4 calls on March 30 (7:41am, 12:15pm, 4:30pm and 6:45pm) and 5 calls on March 31 (7:55am, 11:00am, 2:20pm, 5:05pm and 7:10pm). They also show a call on April 1 at 12:05pm that was answered and lasted 2 minutes.

The calls before 8am: Two of those calls, on March 30 at 7:41am and March 31 at 7:55am, were logged before 8am. The records don't show a time zone, so we can't say whether those times were before 8am where you are. If you tell us your time zone, we'll take that into account.

Your requests for mail-only contact: We couldn't find any request from you to be contacted only by mail in the account history we reviewed. The only mailed contact on file is a notice dated March 2. We also can't see what was said on the April 1 call, because the records don't include what was discussed. This means we can't confirm that those requests were made, and we can't tell you that a change to how you're contacted has been put in place.

Your fear of answering the phone: We heard this, and we know how much it weighs on you. Nothing in the call records speaks to this point, so we have no finding to report on it.

What happens next: Please tell us when and how you asked for mail-only contact, for example the dates, whether it was by phone or in writing, and who you spoke with if you remember. Anything else you think is relevant is welcome too. You can send more information at any time, and we'll review whatever you send. You can reply to this message or call us at the number on your account.

Case reference: 20962593.
